transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because it’s been getting harder since I’ve had to be more in front of people at work. I keep focusing on this one part of my face that looks uneven to me, especially in photos. Other people tell me they barely notice anything, but I can’t stop staring at it.
How much does this concern about your face bother you when you're at work or in social situations?

It bothers me a lot at work. Like, I’ve missed part of a planning deadline because I got stuck spending so much time worrying about how I looked in the event materials. And even normal things like vendor calls or meeting prep take longer than they should because I keep getting distracted by it.
Do you find yourself avoiding social situations or interactions because of your concern about how your face looks?
I’m not totally sure. I mean, I don’t always skip things, but I do hesitate more if I know people will be looking at me. Sometimes I’ll try to keep it brief or stay more in the background.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, taking lots of photos, or trying to cover up that part of your face, because of your concern about how it looks?

Yes. I check my face a lot in my phone camera, especially before I send out event pictures or get on a vendor meeting. I’ll retake photos over and over, or tilt my head a certain way so it looks less uneven. Sometimes I ask a coworker if I look weird, and it can take up enough time that I end up falling behind on planning things.
Do you believe that this part of your face looks abnormal or defective in a way that other people don’t seem to notice?

Yes. I feel like it looks uneven or wrong, especially in photos, and I get stuck staring at it. Other people tell me they barely notice anything, but to me it feels really obvious. It’s gotten worse since I’ve had to be more in front of people at work.
